analysis: The closest option uses sociology, organisational psychology, leadership, negotiation and governance to address coordination of social responses. Public economics and microeconomics support institutional analysis. Survey research, behavioural statistics, econometrics and qualitative methods provide sustained empirical skills. Accounting adds financial literacy; public international law is a closer match to the external law requirement than the previous constitutional course.

The international-policy option studies rights, public and EU law, political institutions and policy, with historical and social inquiry. Public Policy Analysis replaces warfare history to make policy decisions more central. Peace & Conflict, Human Rights and social movements give substance to displacement and social justice; the degree does not become specialist migration studies or humanitarian operations training.

The sustainability and enterprise option joins customer research, venture and product design, digital change and governance with social inquiry. Introduction to Sociology, Social Movements & Environmental Justice and Microeconomics & Behavior replace recycling laboratory work, farming and renewable-system engineering. The remaining scientific foundations, climate and life-cycle analysis support informed product and sustainability decisions. The contributions of general business courses are bounded to enterprise development and decision-making.

All four original offering conflicts are repaired through rescheduling and reassessment. The three options meet the numerical distinctness floor and maintain different organising questions. Alignments reflect concrete overlaps in sociology, psychology, methods, accounting, law, change and survey work. Specialist project-management and wicked-problems units, cross-cultural HRM and the thesis remain unpaired. Optional UCR research is outside the scheduled 180 EC.

Both examine organisational change. UCR focuses on digital strategy and transformation.
